elements.element: Vendor may audit no more than once in any 12-month period.
elements.evidence: The clause permits inspection "no more than once per year," which does not expressly impose a rolling 12-month limit.

elements.element: Vendor must give at least 30 days' written notice of an audit.
elements.evidence: HDI must provide "no less than thirty (30) days prior written notice" to the Company.
Inspection is limited to the Company's normal business hours.

elements.element: Audits are conducted by an independent auditor.
elements.evidence: The inspection right is granted directly to HDI's General Manager, with no independent-auditor requirement.

elements.element: The auditor is bound by confidentiality obligations.
elements.evidence: The clause imposes no confidentiality obligation on the person conducting the inspection.

elements.element: Audits are conducted off-site where possible.
elements.evidence: The clause contains no off-site inspection requirement or preference.

elements.element: Vendor bears audit costs unless underpayment exceeds 5 percent.
elements.evidence: All inspection fees incurred by HDI are borne by HDI, with no underpayment-based cost shifting; this is at least as protective of the Company as the stated exception.

elements.element: Vendor has no direct access to Customer systems for an audit.
elements.evidence: No prohibition on direct access to Company systems is included, and the inspection right is not limited to delivered records or reports.

elements.element: Vendor may audit no more than once per year.
elements.evidence: The clause expressly limits inspection to "no more than once per year."

elements.element: Vendor must give at least 15 days' notice of an audit.
elements.evidence: The required 30 days' prior written notice exceeds the 15-day minimum.

elements.element: Vendor bears audit costs unless underpayment exceeds 10 percent.
elements.evidence: All inspection fees incurred by HDI are borne by HDI, with no underpayment-based cost shifting; this is more protective than permitting cost shifting above 10 percent.
